memo.verdict: Neutral; park; conviction medium. CVS Group at 1221p (24 Sep 2026) is a capital-allocation case dressed as a regulatory-clearing case and is not compelling: the modal return is about 7.6 percent a year over eighteen months and 6.8 percent a year over three years against the 20 percent bar. The park is on the framework's gate rule: trackability ('Leading indicators') is a D because the series that decide the case are semi-annual, and the record does not argue otherwise. Conditions named: the modal path clears the bar below about 1050p on our earnings, about 1100p to 1150p if a reader credits consensus or the five-year median multiple. The two dated triggers that could re-rate the shares are the H1 FY2027 like-for-like print on 4 Mar 2027 and the chief executive appointment; a well-received operator named before the print, with the print at 3 percent or better, is the branch in which we would be wrong quickly (shares at 1485p to 1600p within eighteen months). Invalidate level: like-for-like growth below 0 percent.
case: The thesis as a colleague could repeat it: CVS Group is a capital-allocation case dressed as a regulatory-clearing case, and at 1221p it is not compelling. The regulator has gone and the multiple did not move, because the organic engine stalled and the chief executive is leaving; what remains is £70.0m of buybacks and £50.0m a year of acquisitions turning 2 percent organic growth into about 7 percent a year of adjusted earnings-per-share growth, which at 12.2x earnings pays about 8 percent a year against the 20 percent bar.

1. The change now acting is internal and financial, not operational. Three internal forces are strong on the framework's screen, and all three are uses of capital: £70.0m of buybacks in twelve months retiring about 8 percent of the £832m market capitalisation at about 12x; acquisitions restarted at about £50.0m a year (Australia at about 6x EBITDA, 61 sites; the first UK deal since the regulatory pause, a two-site nine-vet practice for an initial £15.0m); leverage deliberately raised to 1.63x on a £350.0m facility refinanced to 2030. The red-flag check passes except for a soft flag (the buyback is partly debt-funded). 'Internal forces' B; not A because none of the forces lifts the operating outputs, not C because the money is being spent.
counter_case: At its strongest: the shares are a private-market arbitrage with a catalyst. The whole group trades at about 7x EV/EBITDA (an enterprise value of £990m on FY2026 EBITDA of £142m; Deutsche Bank's 7.6x), below the 9x to 10x paid for UK practices, the 10x received for Crematoria in 2025 and the 6x CVS itself pays for sub-scale Australian clinics before synergies. The buyback retires 8 percent of the equity at that multiple. The regulator is gone with no structural remedy, so UK acquisitions resume at reset vendor expectations. Australia compounds from about £20m of EBITDA towards the £105m to £135m+ the company and Deutsche Bank describe. The subscription base (£95.5m, +3.5 percent) and referral demand are defensive. Seven of nine brokers say Buy with a median target of £16.00, 29 percent above the price. The three-year earnings-per-share decline was three external shocks (cyber, regulator, payroll tax), all past. On consensus earnings per share (+11 percent, +9 percent, +7 percent) and a re-rating to 14x to 15x the return is 25 percent a year, an A. Converium Capital made this case in May 2026, and the board's £50.0m buyback half-conceded it.

At the 'Foundations': the foundations are B-grade, not C. A 16.4 percent return on capital employed, 44 percent gross margins, a subscription lock-in on over 40 percent of active patients, a laboratory with margins over 30 percent, a rational oligopoly and a settled regulator; the earnings decline was a cyber attack (about £7m of revenue and £4.2m to £5m of cost), a regulator and a payroll-tax rise, all external and all past.
triggers: - UK like-for-like growth: our modal 2.5 percent for H1 FY2027 (4 Mar 2027) and 2 to 3 percent for FY2027; alarm below 1.5 percent; invalidate below 0 percent; upgrade trigger at or above 3 percent for two halves with members stable; a negative half would mark the 10.80x branch. Guidance 4 to 8 percent; consensus revenue +4.9 percent FY2027. The four-month trading update in November 2026 comes first.

- The chief executive appointment: probable by mid-2027 (75 percent); alarm a caretaker or a further finance-track hire; upgrade a multi-site or clinical operator, which alone would move our modal multiple to 12.5x to 13x; a well-received name before the H1 FY2027 print, with the print at 3 percent or better, is the branch in which we are wrong quickly (1485p to 1600p within eighteen months).
- Healthy Pet Club members: our modal 500,000 to 510,000 from 508,000; alarm below 500,000; Healthy Pet Club Advanced adoption is one of the research's four thesis-changing data points.

- Cash conversion and leverage: our modal 70 to 74 percent and 1.7x to 1.9x; alarm below 70 percent, or above 2.0x without a named acquisition; cash conversion back above 75 percent would ease the adverse drop-through; leverage through 2.0x would mark it.

- Acquisitions: UK entry multiples our modal 8x to 9x, alarm above 10x; Australian disclosed multiples alarm above 8x, or a deployment pause under the new chief executive; our modal about 70 Australian sites and £25m of pre-overhead EBITDA by June 2027; £50.0m a year at a blended 7x or below likely (60 percent).
- The buyback: about £18m left to complete in FY2027; a halt by the new chief executive costs about 2 percent of earnings per share.

judgement.heading: CVS Group | Middle Innings Core Investment, sell signal, held under your one-off in/out link | 2.50% of the fund's capital in 2 tranches | third in the order of sale
judgement.markdown:
- **Industry:** CVS Group is in Healthcare. Healthcare's Industry RS was 79 at the Friday 23 October reading (53 four weeks earlier)
- **Sector:** CVS Group is in Hospitals, clinics and care homes. That sector's Sector RS was 32 at the 30 September month-end (46 at the August month-end); on Friday's daily reading it was 58
  - The sector's other companies, with their daily Stock RS: Fresenius Medical Care (42), Medicover (87), Emeis (4), Attendo (85), Clariane (8), Diagnostyka (24), and 6 more
- **Cohort:** CVS Group is in Private hospital, clinic, lab and vet networks. The cohort's relative strength was 58 on Friday's daily reading (54 four weeks earlier). The cohort's other companies: Medicover (87), Diagnostyka (24), Aevis Victoria (60), Spire Healthcare (79), Terveystalo (5)
- **CVS Group's charts are on CVS Group's page on the PMS Per-stock Dashboard:** https://vfhqi.github.io/ratings/pms/holding.html?t=CVSG-GB

**What is going on, and why it matters**
- **The price move, by beta:** over twenty sessions CVS Group's shares rose about 9%; CVS Group's beta of 1.11 explains almost none of it, so CVS Group's own move was about +10%, 1.6 times its usual size, larger than usual. I found no public news that explains the CVS Group rise
- **The sector:** CVS Group's sector's companies fell about 6% over the same twenty sessions, so the CVS Group rise is CVS Group's own, against a falling sector
- **The analysts:** for CVS Group, Net Upgrade Breadth, sales estimates was +22% and Net Upgrade Breadth, target prices 0% at the 30 September month-end

**What it means for the position**
- **Holding:** only your one-off in/out link holds CVS Group; two Sell Criteria are met
- **Selling:** CVS Group goes when the third purchase releases it; on Friday's daily readings the Sell Criterion of Sector RS below 50 together with Stock RS below 70 is likely to stop being met at the 30 October month-end, while the 200-day average of CVS Group's relative price (-1.6% over the month) keeps one Sell Criterion met
- **Adding:** not allowed, because CVS Group meets a Sell Criterion
- **CVS Group's place in the order of sale:** third, behind Theon and Bally's Intralot, because the memo's park on CVS Group is on trackability, not on the quality gate of management or business quality
  - A four-week rise of about 9% with no news behind it is a better price to sell at, not a reason to keep

**What we could lose:** about 0.73% of the fund's capital, if CVS Group's price falls to its 30% level at about 929.6p

**Experiment: which stocks CVS Group's own moves have tracked** (last 3 and 6 months)
- **Energean** (same country of listing): 0.37 and 0.11, weak
- **Kingfisher** (same country of listing): 0.36 and 0.21, weak
- **British American Tobacco** (same country of listing): 0.33 and 0.17, weak
- **Experian** (same country of listing): 0.28 and 0.28, weak
- **My reading:** CVS Group's moves are mostly its own

**The Investment Analyst's memo on CVS Group (1 October, at 1,221p; digest of 25 September)**
- **Decided:** the memo on CVS Group parks the case, neutral, medium conviction, on the framework's gate rule for trackability (rated D, because the series that decide the case are reported only twice a year)
- **Must happen:** United Kingdom like-for-like growth of 3% or more for two halves, and a chief executive appointment of a multi-site or clinical operator
- **Main risk:** the organic engine has stalled, leaving a capital-allocation case of buybacks and acquisitions
- **Expected return (the Modal return):** about 7.6% a year over eighteen months; the memo clears our bar of 20% a year only below about 1,050p, about 20% below Friday's close of 1,317p
- **Next test:** the first-half like-for-like print on 4 March 2027, or the chief executive appointment if it comes first

**My judgement:** bearish on the CVS Group position (sell third), medium conviction
- The memo's return is well under half our bar and the rise has no public explanation, so the case for keeping CVS Group rests only on the readings improving
- **Counter-case:** if both of CVS Group's Sell Criteria clear by mid-November, CVS Group becomes a Middle Innings Core Investment with no sell signal in an industry (Healthcare) that just moved into the market's top quarter

**What would change my view:** a chief executive appointment from an operating background; the 200-day average of CVS Group's relative price turning up at a Friday reading

bullets.text: CVS Group is a Middle Innings Core Investment, so its MA SLs sell nothing; its six Sell Criteria decide the sale.
CVS Group's 50D MA SL exit was confirmed on 25-Sep for both tranches, and CVS Group closed 5.9% above its 1,242.6p stop on 27-Oct.
A CVS Group fall of 5.6% from the 27-Oct close of 1,316p would take CVS Group's SP back to its 1,242.6p stop.

items.criterion: The 200D MA of relative price flat or falling over the month, read each Friday

bullets.text: Sell signal: CVS Group's relative 200D MA fell (1.62%) over the month to 27-Oct, more steeply than the (0.76%) of 25-Sep.
Even a 12.6% CVS Group rise to about 1,481p, held from 28-Oct, would end the sell signal from CVS Group's relative 200D MA only at the 27-Nov reading.
Under your one-off in/out link, the whole CVS Group holding (2.50% of capital) sells when its replacement is bought, fourth in my proposed order of sale.

bullets.text: CVS Group's Sector RS of 32 with Stock RS of 39 at the 30-Sep month-end is a sell signal, but CVS Group's Sector RS reads 56 on 27-Oct.
A CVS Group Sector RS of 50 or more at the Friday 30-Oct month-end ends the Sector RS sell signal, but CVS Group still sells on its relative 200D MA.
CVS Group's Sector RS reverses fast, having reached 50 or more at only 3 of 12 Friday readings since 7-Aug.

bullets.text: No sell signal: CVS Group's PT Net Upgrade Breadth is (18%) on 27-Oct, below zero, but CVS Group's Stock RS is 51, 2 points above the line.
CVS Group's Stock RS has been 50 or more at only 3 of 30 Friday readings since 20-Mar.
A CVS Group Stock RS of 49 or lower at Friday 30-Oct gives a sell signal, a third for a holding already awaiting replacement.

items.criterion: Relative price more than 25% below its 52W high, read at the month-end

bullets.text: No sell signal: CVS Group's relative price is 13.6% below its 52W high on 27-Oct, against the 25% line.
CVS Group's relative price was 24.8% below its 52W high at 30-Sep, and less than half of the improvement since is CVS Group's own outperformance.
At a flat market, a CVS Group month-end close below about 1,142.3p, only 2.3p above the 2-Oct low close of 1,140p, gives a sell signal.

Low: CVS Group's Industry RS would need to fall about 50 points to give a sell signal, which is unlikely by Friday 30-Oct.

adds.criterion: The rules: no sell signal from the six Sell Criteria

bullets.text: CVS Group has two sell signals: a falling relative 200D MA (down 1.6% over the month at 23-Oct) and Sector RS 32 with Stock RS 39 at 30-Sep.
With a sell signal on, the rules allow no add to CVS Group, and the whole CVS Group holding awaits replacement under your one-off in/out link.

CVS Group's 50D, 150D and 200D MAs are falling, and your 22-Sep negatives still hold: "the 150D MA is below the 200D MA" and the "150D MA is declining".
A CVS Group pullback that holds its rising 100D MA (1,254.97p on 27-Oct) without closing more than 2% below it, with the 200D MA turning up.
